Could solar powered autonomous airships be cheaper taxis than cars? Discuss!

I ran the numbers on hydrogen powered personal air ships for commuting into LA. One-person capacity.

Before government intervention, they would cost about $40,000 just to fill up. They take up tons of space and are generally a clusterfuck.

They aren't very quick, but they are faster than LA gridlock.

Maybe if some quality engineering were done we could bring the price point down, but at a glance they are a terrible option.

Also, a version with the same carrying capacity as a bus would be a nightmare to load and unload in the city.

It's funny how this post got very little discussion. Over the long term, the answer is definitely yes. A solar powered airship would only have a couple of moving parts, and they are the kind of moving parts that could be designed to last nearly forever with no maintenance. Hydrogen could be mined directly out of water vapor out of the air, as needed. All the other parts could be buy once and then forget it. Buses are a terrible idea for airships. Smaller 2-4 person airships make a lot more sense. And taking up space shouldn't matter at all. They would only be near the ground long enough for passengers to embark and then disembark. Thereafter they'd be floating around, or tethered collecting solar and wind energy waiting for the next Uber style call.

On a longer time line, solar powered airships beat out every transportation option, cost wise. Zero infrastructure is a HUGE savings. Think about how much it costs to maintain roads and rail road tracks... Or how much maintenance boats and ports require...

You make a point I hadn't considered. A "cloud" of airships responding to smartphone calls could dramatically increase "ownership efficiency." Basically, an individual would not have to burden the full cost of airship ownership.

However, mining hydrogen from water vapor isn't realistic. The production rate would be too low and the extra equipment would cut into the carrying capacity of the vehicles. Likewise, solar panels would be a questionable decision. A chemical motor would probably have lower weight than the batteries and panels.
